newsitem.title: USA: U.S. benefits offices beef up security amid cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. benefits offices beef up security amid cuts.

text.p: Social Security offices in four Midwest states were beefing up security Thursday to guard against possible violence when people find out their benefits have been cut, an agency official said.

Armed guards were being posted at about 45 of the 80 field offices in Kansas, Missouri, Iowa and Nebraska as the Social Security Administration gets ready to implement new federal legislation. Guards had previously been on duty at only a handful of those offices.

Bud Nolker of SSA regional headquarters in Kansas City said people who claim disability because of drug and alcohol abuse after Jan. 1 will no longer be eligible for Supplemental Security Income benefits. Later next year, the government will cut off similar payments to resident aliens.
"We're concerned that these folks could become very upset," Nolker said. He added that other regions will likely act in a similar way to prevent possible violence.
